logs.comments: Lyrics are definitely a little weird in isolation but they fit well with the vibe of the song. Lyrics are a little repetitive and the song doesn't really go anywhere
The song is very long and meanders a bit. The sections that are clearly designed for dance breaks in a live performance don't help the flow either.
logs.songName: The Way You Make Me Feel - 2012 Remaster

logs.comments: Nice outro. Kind of saves the flow. Could argue that vocal score should be higher.
Some of the sections are a little odd. You could argue that the vocal score should be higher.
The structure is really interesting with the interlude and the refrain. Overall just melds together very well, rapping is well executed, lyrics are a bit random but the words "sound" good.
The vocals are nice but almost a little too breathy even if that's the intended style.
logs.songName: What Was I Made For? [From The Motion Picture "Barbie"]

logs.comments: Bridge is outstanding and the final chorus concludes the song well. Some of the sections have vocals that are so unique and flawless I can't begin to imagine executing them
The second verse is really good. The added vocals in the final chorus and the outro help the flow a lot.
The vocals are excellent but they do stick out a little bit. I actually love the background vocals in the outro.
Flow is barely passable. There is building in the background and some variation but still the chorus is repetitive.
Background vocals do a lot for this song
I really like his flow (lyrical flow and overall song flow are different). The background is actually pretty interesting too, some pretty unique chords there
This was a really difficult song to grade. Still don't really know how to approach it
Also has an amazing music video. I think on paper the structure with 3 different verses from 2 different perspectives moving into "all the same" at the end is cool. The execution feels a bit flat.
I was bit on the fence about vocals lyrics and flow here. Vocals are solid but nothing really pops out. Some words and phrases are repetitive and the song stays at the same energy level throughout.
Pretty uninspiring structure. Not much motion throughout the song.
The execution almost sounds too clean for the vibe of the song
Lyrics are very simple. Nothing to dislike that much I guess. Funnily enough the one part I feel is a bit out of place is line the song is named after.
I keep hearing "que paso" at the start of the chorus
Emotion in lyrics and background feels incongruent. Vocals are emotional and the background feels very "chill" and "vibey." The water sound is also a bit intrusive

logs.songName: テレフォン・ナンバー
logs.comments: Had to deduct a bit for the lyrics. 56709 is repeated a lot and it's just not a great lyric. Still kind of works though
I love these vocals. Filled with emotion. The second chorus peaks much higher than the first. I don't know Japanese but the words sound good and the translation looks fine
Vocals are unpolished but have a lot of emotion. The song is very repetitive though.
Vocals are unpolished but have a lot of emotion. The song is very repetitive though.
The background does build. I still would've preferred some new lyrics and a bit more of a climax.
I do like how the instruments come in during the second half, and how the song concludes the way it started.
Gorgeous instrumental, blends beautifully. Lyrics read like a poem.
logs.songName: 浪子心聲 - 電影《半斤八両》歌曲

logs.comments: The background builds a bit. You could argue the background score should be higher.
Seems like a lot of canto pop songs have the formula of slowly adding instruments to make the next chorus peak higher. Not the most revolutionary but definitely not bad.
Gorgeous background. Creates such powerful emotions. Clear lows and highs throughout. Maybe a slight criticism that the low high low high low high low high pattern can start to wear a bit.

I really like this song. I like it more than the score I gave it. Her style is just so odd to grade because her singing is off key but it seems intentional. Even so, in parts like the second chorus it just sounds off-putting.
The song clearly builds throughout. Some really nice lyrics in here like "this all-consuming fire fuming" but also some weaker ones like "what's going on" which doesn't sound right.
Definitely one of my favorite background instrumentals

My favorite song. I think it sounds much better when you turn up the volume, otherwise you can't hear all the details in the background. The song has obvious climaxes and the second chorus peaks higher than the first.
The peak in the second verse is incredible. Main criticism is how often the chorus repeats, especially at the end. Just not a very strong ending.

logs.songName: CAN'T STOP THE FEELING! (from DreamWorks Animation's "TROLLS")
logs.comments: The bass does a lot for this song. The parts all fit well with the upbeat theme. Very repetitive stuff though, the refrain, pre-chorus, chorus and post-chorus all are almost one to one.
Cohesion score might be too high on this one

I can't understand the lyrics but I like how all the sections are distinct. The translated lyrics also seem very sad and sweet. I like how the song transitions into "if she comes back" and that the outro calls back to the prior phrase
Crazy falsetto. I absolutely love the instrumental on this one but the score might be a bit high.
Crazy falsetto. I absolutely love the instrumental on this one but the score might be a bit high.

"My favorite song. I think it sounds much better when you turn up the volume, otherwise you can't hear all the details in the background. The song has obvious climaxes and the second chorus peaks higher than the first. "
Background grows throughout. I don't like the line "that's what friends are s'posed to do" line but the lyrics overall are solid.

Putting different parts on different sides has an interesting effect but it does feel a bit lacking in the left ear. The lyrics sound poetic but are a bit nonsensical. I'm tempted to increase the vocal score because his voice has such a unique quality.

I feel that the "ooh, baby, baby" kind of breaks the flow a bit and the transition into the instrumental was a bit random but the song moves smoothly mostly. Instrumental on this song is amazing and everything fits together well.
The lyrics on this one are a bit basic. "You're a teaser you turn 'em on" is a bit of a clunky line. Arguably could be decreased.
Cohesion score might be too high on this one
The piano accompaniment fits really well with the vocals. Vocals feel very free and unleashed. Lyrics fit well with the theme but can be a little silly and they repeat.
Unreal vocals. I think the key change stuff at the end is interesting but it gets a little repetitive and the fade out ending feels lazy
The first half flows really well with the two unique verses but it repeats the post chorus too many times at the end I feel.

I really don't like the bridge. I think it completely ruins the vibe of the song for me as something very bittersweet. Aside from that I really like how the song sounds a bit confused on whether it's a bit more upbeat or melancholy. Kind of like denial?
Really beautiful lyrics in the context that they're about his mother's death. The way the chorus is delivered is different each time.
A lot of unique lyrics. One of the few ELO songs where the vocals are really highlighted. There's clearly a flow in the lyrics with this "voyage." The song has clear lows and highs.

Very short and simple in terms of flow and lyrics. I didn't want to lower lyric score since the song is so short anyway, but you could argue they repeat and are overly simplistic. I thought it was fine.

Lyrics are a mixed bag. I don't really like "case of fragile glass," I think it's too direct. "A year and forty days since you picked me up and swept me away" is very specific and the rhyming feels tacky.
Lyrics are a bit repetitive but the delivery is different.
That last crazy turn at the end sounded a bit out of control to me. I feel like the instrumental is lacking a bit of percussion. Lyrics sound good but they are a bit repetitive.
Lyrics are lighthearted and whimsical which matches with the song. The outro is great, background vocals especially feel like the missing piece.

logs.songName: It's Been a Long, Long Time
logs.comments: Might just be the mixing but it feels like there's a hole in the lower sounds. Lyrics are brief, nothing wrong or special. Flow is actually good, the repeated verse at the end concludes lyrics well and the background wraps up beautifully.

logs.songName: I Want To Break Free - Remastered 2011
logs.comments: Unsure if I like how different the feeling of the lyrics are from the vocals or not, it definitely has its charm. The distinct verses definitely indicate flow over time of getting over someone. Very conflicted over scores for almost every category here.

The quality of her voice is really good for this song. I admittedly don't like how much the chorus repeats. Some of the lyrics are good, others are a little corny.  It feels like there was the idea to have the song build a lot but it never got there.
I wish there were more unique verses man.

Vocals are a little odd, might be an acquired taste. Background is uninspiring for most of the song except for the bridge. You could argue all the parts fit together with the theme? Overall, a very weird song to grade, very unconventional.
The back and forth conversation is cool. The lyrics indicate a flow a time with an event happening at the bridge.
The parts blend well. You can feel that the song has a direction as it rises and falls.

The whole song has this slurred grungy feeling that really feels like the vibe of a stumbling drunk. The emotions reach their peak by the fourth verse. Lyrics are a little all over the place. I guess that also fits with the rest of the song.

Vocals feel very technical. Really nice lyrics, as expected since it's a jazz standard. The song has a rising and falling motion. Nothing special about cohesion I don't think, the background mostly is just getting out of the way of the vocals.
Love the instrumental. A lot of chorus but the delivery does vary a bit. I really like the verse with "how can you stay."

I'm a little biased with this song admittedly. I really like the line starting with "you reach your hand to hold me." The energy of the song increases throughout. One of the best implementations of having different parts in different ears.
Blends well. Lyrics fit with a consistent theme. I guess some of the wording in the lyrics is a bit pedestrian, could lower the score. The song has clear lows and highs giving it motion.
Shocking good vocals, very technical. Pretty disastrous lyrics. Repetitive, boring and crude. Flow is actually pretty cool with the extra parts coming in later in the song.
Background vocals are a bit too aggressive in my opinion. I like the consistency each verse has with the river theme. They are iterate upon it a bit. Lyrics follow a similar structure and theme.

logs.songName: Rocket Man (I Think It's Going To Be A Long, Long Time)
logs.comments: The sounds in the background (synth?) together with the background vocals give it a mellow "spacey" sound that fits with the theme. I like how it switches between isolating his vocals and blending with the full background. Gives it a lonely sound.
I really like the lines "Come back and haunt me" and "do not speak as loud as my heart." The song builds upwards throughout.

I like how the final "anyway" calls back to the one from the end of the first verse. Good example of varying repetitions, the second chorus has a lot more energy than the first. The song has some direction as it flares up then dies down.
The song has a kind of "fuzzy" sound that makes you feel the idea of something stumbling around in a haze. The outro calls back to the first verse which is nice.

Some lyrics like "Emerald Bar" are a bit random. It's a story about a character but the song is too short to flesh it out. I do like the simplicity of the chorus lyrics and lines like "you've got not real ambition" though.

Mikky's vocals sound a little tense. I actually like the way the chorus differs each time it comes. It swaps singers for the second chorus and Rhianna adds a spectacular embellishment to the final one for the outro.

logs.songName: Take Me Home, Country Roads - Original Version
logs.comments: Background vocals are really nice when you listen closely. Incredible lyrics in the unique verses and the bridge. I think there's at least one additional part every time the chorus comes back as well.
Not a huge fan of Earl Sweatshirt's verse. The verse with the "I'm on that ledge" line is really good. Lyrics are consistent with a theme that also has a bit of a story which gives it good flow.
Not a huge fan of Earl Sweatshirt's verse. The verse with the "I'm on that ledge" line is really good. Lyrics are consistent with a theme that also has a bit of a story which gives it good flow.

Mikky's vocals sound a little tense. I actually like the way the chorus differs each time it comes. It swaps singers for the second chorus and Rhianna adds a spectacular embellishment to the final one for the outro.

Third verse indicates time passing which helps flow. I think the final chorus would've been better if it was more unique. Arguably could lower vocal score, it's not the most impressive performance but I like the emotion.

The vocals have a sound (an echo?) that makes them feel so lonely. Incredibly iconic piano riff. The first time the pre-chorus comes is amazing, it's a great transition into the higher energy section. I wish the second half didn't repeat so much stuff.

The vocals have a sound (an echo?) that makes them feel so lonely. Incredibly iconic piano riff. The first time the pre-chorus comes is amazing, it's a great transition into the higher energy section. I wish the second half didn't repeat so much stuff.
Chorus makes up too much of the song I feel. The timbre of his voice is incredible though. It blends well with the background vocals and the guitar.
Some good lyrics, others a bit awkward or cheesy. Too much chorus. Instrumental is very cool.
I like the lyrics in the first two verses a lot. The vocals very dynamic which makes the lyrics feel less repetitive, especially in the outro.

The lyrics just start repeating in the second half. Granted, the execution is different, but not having any new unique lyrics feels like a mistake. I debated on raising the background score, still not sure.
I like the way the parts blend. I also quite like the flow of the song, the transitions from the instrumental sections to the vocal sections is nice.

I'm not a huge fan of the guitar solo, it feels a bit out of place with the other instruments and the rest of the song. The lyrics sound good and the translation seems good. The final chorus peaks the highest and adds more parts which helps the flow.
The reversed vocals at the bridge is a little tacky. The chorus repeats a lot but some of the lyrics are also pretty nice so it about evens out. Vocals in the final chorus are absolutely gorgeous.
Beautiful story in the lyrics that has a clear flow of time.
Beautiful story in the lyrics that has a clear flow of time.
logs.songName: When She Loved Me - From "Toy Story 2" / Soundtrack Version

logs.comments: Four distinct verses and each one has lyrics that express powerful feelings of grief and sorrow. A lot of chorus admittedly. There are ups and downs in the song but overall it climbs to the climax in the outro. The percussion in the background is great.

Lyrics are beautiful and haunting. I do almost feel like the last chorus went the wrong way maybe. I think it should've quietly died down instead of trying to climax. Strangely Spotify says the line is "dry as the walls" instead of "white as the walls."
The vocals carry a lot of emotion. Lyrics are beautiful. Small criticism, the transition from "wish you were here" to "we're just two lost souls" is a bit awkward.

logs.songName: Take Me Home, Country Roads - Original Version
logs.comments: Background vocals are really nice when you listen closely. Incredible lyrics in the unique verses and the bridge. I think there's at least one additional part every time the chorus comes back as well.
The background is unbelievably repetitive which also makes the song a bit repetitive despite the changing lyrics
Very little variation in the lyrics
Not a fan of the line "as the atom bomb locks in" but a lot of the other lyrics are nice.
I like the first section a lot more than the rest
All the parts fit together well with the theme of the song. Some of the sections feel a bit odd or exhausting though because it's a very a long song so I reduced the flow.
Flow score reduced because I feel like the bridge doesn't fit perfectly and because the song keeps the same format until the last verse

Difficult song to grade. I kind of just don't like repeated sections. Maybe it's because of the energy level of the song but I feel like even one direct repetition has me wonder a bit why I'm listening to the same thing again.

Not personally a huge fan of this song but it does a lot of things right. The flow is great because of the theme of age and it also calls back to the beginning at the end. This also gives it a lot of unique lyrics. I'm probably underrating it because of my bias.
A surprisingly good song? Although the chorus repeats a lot, the execution varies and more parts are added throughout the song.
First verse has good lyrics but most of the rest are repetitive and mediocre. Nothing too wrong with the vocals but they're just a bit boring. Instrument break and the bridge feel a bit out of place.
Juxtaposition between the two section is pretty cool. It does mess with the flow a little bit though, makes the song feel kind of choppy.
A bit repetitive.

logs.artists: Metro Boomin, Swae Lee, Lil Wayne, Offset
logs.comments: Lyrics generally aren't saying anything, there are also a lot of words relating to the movie. Some cool riffs in the background but also quite repetitive.
logs.songName: Annihilate (Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse) (Metro Boomin & Swae Lee, Lil Wayne, Offset)

logs.comments: Lyrics are a bit all over the place. Riff is iconic but very little in the background aside from that. The bridge kind of kills that consistent pulse throughout the song. Cohesion is debatable, could go down.
logs.songName: Another One Bites The Dust - Remastered 2011

logs.comments: I like how the last chorus is changed and how the last line calls back to the first.
Not a huge fan of the bridge
Lyrics are pretty simplistic and repetitive.
Lyrics are pretty repetitive
I love that bass riff. Lyrics get repetitive towards the end, basically just repeating the same lines. Vocals are "immature" which is a stylistic choice but I still think the score should be lowered.

logs.artists: Jessie J, Ariana Grande, Nicki Minaj
logs.comments: Very impressive vocals actually. Lyrics are crass but that's very consistent with the rest of the song and some of the lines are pretty creative.
Personally I think the lyrics are kind of a vibe but objectively they are repetitive and nonsensical.
A lot of the lyrics feel vague or erratic.
The peak in the last chorus is nice. I think you could argue for a lot of the scores here to be increased.
Lyrics are repetitive and crass but vocals are good. Bridge is pretty meh.
The chorus is always exactly the same and the lyrics in the rap verses feel overly crude. It feels like there was some unexplored potential with the bittersweet sound in the chorus.
Background feels very basic, could have a lower score. Chorus is very similar aside from a few added parts in the background every time.
Chorus is very repetitive and background is boring. Vocals, especially in the second half, are absolutely gorgeous.

This song does a lot of things well but it just repeats the chorus too much in the second half. I really like the two unique verses at the beginning, especially the transition at the end of them into the chorus. I also generally like the energy of the song.
I really like the timbre of his voice in this song. I think you could argue the lyrics are a bit basic.

This song is all over the place. The third verse and bridge are completely different and the lyrics are more nonsensical. I do like how it returns to the same theme as the first half at the end though. Scoring on this one is very questionable.
I like the idea but some of the lyrics feel a little too on the nose maybe? The bridge also messes with the consistent rhythm a bit in my opinion, maybe some kind of a dance break?
A lot of distinct verses in the lyrics and there is a story

Lyrics are a little abstract. The song cuts off suddenly because it transitions immediately into the next song in the album but that does make the song worse in isolation. It generally just feels incomplete by itself. Vocals aren't too impressive.

I took a bit off of flow because I didn't like how it transitioned from chorus into an incredibly short bridge back into a chorus that was almost identical. A lot of scores here are on the upper edge though.

Pretty solid song but maybe a bit basic? Words like "stupid" and "dumb" feel a bit pedestrian. Vocals would be a bit better without the slight accent. I like the bridge a lot. I do not like how the song ends suddenly after a repeated chorus.

I really like all the little piano riffs in the background. Maybe slight criticism that there are no lyrics in the scat/instrumental bridge which is the only thing between the repeated chorus but the second chorus has a different mood compared to the first.
I feel like I waited for the song to go somewhere but it never did. Vocals in the first verse were pretty impressive. Background is exceedingly bland.
The melody is incredibly unique and interesting. I don't have a score category to give to that. The song doesn't conclude very well in my opinion, feels unresolved, maybe purposefully?

Small nitpick, I don't like the overlap of the word pain between "heartache from the pain" to the chorus. Instrumental is very basic until the end and I kind of just don't like the sudden back and forth motion between the chorus and the verses.

I like how the chorus varies slightly every time while maintaining some consistency. Some awkward lyrics and choppy phrases. I think by the third time the pattern repeats I'm kind of waiting for it to go somewhere.
Has the same kind of strange choppy back and forth feeling as believer. I dislike it but that might be just preference. I also don't like the bridge.
Feels like the song stopped doing anything new after around the first minute and a half
The first verse into the first chorus is incredible. Then it kind of falls off. I just gave it 8's across the board thinking that the cool stuff cancels out the meh stuff

Might just be a preference but I really don't like these vocals. I don't like how some parts just suddenly cut off and it doesn't sound very well supported. I don't like how the song builds as if it's going to climax then just drops.
Maybe not enough background during the unique verses.
Lyrics feel a little surface level maybe for such a heavy topic. Background is just an infinite loop and it feels more repetitive because it's a sample.
The chorus is pretty corny but I actually like some of the lyrics in unique verses. The bridge also fits in well.
I don't like the kind of techno style that comes in at the second half. Her voice also sounds like it's being garbled by pitch correction.
I generally like this song. I like the line "Oh, what a shame that you came here with someone." Only complaint is that the chorus repeats too often without much variation.

I get that the lyrics are supposedly related to WW2 but some of the word choices aren't great. There's so much focus on the verses that the climax doesn't have lyrics which makes it feel less meaningful?
Bridge was very odd but it transitioned really well into the final chorus.
Bridge is amazing. It suddenly cuts out after the second chorus for some reason. Chorus is maybe a little repetitive.
Some of the lyrics, especially in the pre-choruses, are nice. I do feel like the song doesn't build to anything or have an obvious motion and it ends somewhat abruptly. Background is a little basic.
Maybe a little corny. The delivery of the vocals kind of adds to that. There is a bit of an accent on the male vocals. Lyrics are a little basic and repetitive.

I like the song but it is a little confusing between some of the edgy and nonsensical lyrics and extremely upbeat instrumental. Structure is also a little weird with the repeated "the mask that you wore" section into an instrumental.
Sections connect well. Rapping seems pretty good, maybe a little flat. I don't like the decision to end the song by just repeating the chorus, it feels very boring.
Quite repetitive.

The song actually builds well to the climax. There's a consistent motion throughout the song too. Everything fits together really well during the peaks at the chorus. The repeated sections have their differences too. Bridge is also good.

I don't like some parts of the vocals (you can hear a lot of breath and air) but it's hard to deny that he's a very good singer. Lots of unique lyrics and the translation looks good. This song probably deserves a higher score.
Vocals are a little all over the place. Some of the notes randomly oscillate unnaturally. The timbre of his voice is pretty good in a lot of spots though. The song cuts off very abruptly.

Pretty repetitive chorus. Song also does give a feeling like it went nowhere. It ended pretty much where it started but because that was a repeated section it doesn't have the same impact as a callback.
A bit repetitive. There's only one section (the second verse) that never gets repeated. The peaks of the song sound too similar.
His voice is a little too "bubbly" for me and he enunciates words very firmly. The song is a little chorus heavy but they do differ a bit.
Maybe a few too many repeats of "getting to the point." Lyrics generally are pretty good though.

logs.songName: The Girl Is Mine (with Paul McCartney)
logs.comments: Both vocals are good but to be honest Michael Jackson sounds so effortless while Paul McCartney sounds like he's straining a bit. Some slightly odd lyrics, partially because there's a dialogue but also in words like "doggone."
Vocals are a little angsty, especially the rapping parts. Honestly, I just don't like the rap sections. The peak in the chorus is incredible. Scores kind of end up as an average of the two.

Bass is great at the start. The song peaks well at the chorus. Bridge is good. Callback to the start at the end is nice too. I'm not a huge fan of the immature nature of the vocals and lyrics but I get that it's kind of the point.
Only criticism of the lyrics is that I think the last section at the end could've been its own unique verse instead of repeating the second verse.
Same criticism of Adam Young's vocals, he over pronounces words. I like the high energy of the song. I don't like how there are only two real distinct verses.
Structure is pretty simplistic, just four verses with choruses between them. I didn't deduct from flow because the song is still dominated by distinct verses.
Very simple structure, two verses and two choruses. Maybe missing a clear outro?

The last chorus is delivered differently which is good. I don't really like this song but it's hard to deduct from the score. The lyrics are dramatic and rather shallow and it very much ends where it starts.
In the middle of the last chorus it randomly gets really muffled for some reason?
Way too chorus heavy
It gets a little too upbeat and "poppy" for me later in the song. Kind of kills that beautiful raw emotion you hear in other versions like the one by Jeff Buckley.
Gets very repetitive in the second half. Lyrics in the rap verse are completely unrelated. It feels like there are a few different styles in the background that don't quite fit together.
The background builds throughout the song but it does generally feel very simplistic and underwhelming to me. A dedicated outro would've made this song much better.

Lyrics are a little simplistic. Maybe a bit too much repetition of certain words, even in the unique verses, but generally lyrics are solid. The song doesn't really go anywhere at the end unfortunately.
Really unique melody. Vocals are a little unconventional, you would expect them to be a little more delicate considering the rest of the song. It kind of fits with the background though.

Some pretty cool lyrics here in the first verse and the chorus. I don't like how the third verse just repurposes some previous lyrics. I don't like how they mess with the voice on the response lines like "Oh, brother." It sounds very hollow.
Great bridge. Could make a case to raise the vocal score.
Cute song. I don't like the part at the end where they reverse all the audio.
Chorus gets a little repetitive.
Very few unique lyrics on this one. A lot of "ooh" and "ahh." The lyrics that are there are pretty good though. The choruses are literally identical though.
Very basic lyrics. Ends abruptly.
Not really sure what's up with the percussion on this one. Sounds kind of like what beatboxers are trying to imitate. Maybe a heartbeat? I feel like the last chorus was a strange decision.

logs.artists: Ed Sheeran & Justin Bieber, Justin Bieber
logs.comments: Very choppy lines and background. I actually like the "I always feel like I'm nobody" line. The line "what I'm with my baby, yeah" ending with "yeah" feels so lazy. A bit odd that the two characters in the duet aren't talking about each other.

logs.songName: I Don’t Wanna Live Forever (Fifty Shades Darker)
logs.comments: A bit strange how it builds up to a peak but then the "peak" is actually pretty low energy, and then the next section is a little higher energy? The run that ZAYN goes on in the last chorus sounds a little all over the place.
Did they just invent the phrase "I'm not into bacon?" Lyrics are kind of hilarious but the character is supposed to be upset. Song is very upbeat? Bridge is great.

Vocals are a little underwhelming, I wish he gave it as much as he did in the outro for the rest of the song. I love how many unique verses there are, generally I like the lyrics. The piano solos are really good.

I like how the instruments get added one by one. Bass drop was pretty underwhelming. Bridge moves into the last chorus well. I like the added backing vocals in the last chorus. Chorus does feel a little out of place and is just lacking bass.
Very nonsensical lyrics. Ends pretty suddenly.
Very angsty lyrics, I get a lot of secondhand embarrassment.
The song drags on a bit with the audio from what I assume is the birth of his child playing, which is also too loud.
Rikrok's voice is too sweet for the incredibly crass lyrics. Bridge is good. I like how there's a kind of story arc and character development of sorts.
Quite repetitive. Bridge is a little odd? Key change?
logs.songName: I Wanna Dance with Somebody (Who Loves Me)

logs.comments: I would like if there was some more emotion in the vocals. I think one problem with groups of singers is they all get detached from the song. The lyrics recycle the same few lines repeatedly. The final chorus is pretty nice.

logs.songName: It's Still Rock and Roll to Me

logs.comments: The high energy is great. All parts of the song are on the same page about that. A few too many lyrics are some variation of the name of the song. There are a few lines I don't like such as "kickstart my heart, give it a start" which repeats "start."
Not too much going in the lyrics or flow but the instrumental is pretty infectious.
Repetitive and dominated by the chorus. Lyrics are pretty basic.
Lyrics are pretty basic. The "I got me a therapist" feels very cramped.
Not sure if it's just my headphones but the percussive sounds are way to loud and stick out. Four repetitions of the chorus is a lot. The first and last are different I guess.

Vocals are a little too aggressive in the pre-chorus I feel, especially after the intro was very calm. It does feel a little odd how it peaks in the pre-chorus then goes down for the actual chorus? Background feels very basic.

logs.songName: Like I'm Gonna Lose You (feat. John Legend)
logs.comments: A LOT of repetition in the lyrics. They do change the way they sing the chorus though. I almost think vocal score could be higher.

That "craving" stuck out a lot lol. His voice sounds a bit timid, which suits a lot of the song but not some of these aggressive entrances. Some strange choices for the melody at the bridge? I like that I can feel what he was going for.
I can't believe that's the first line. Considering that there's an actual story in the lyrics I kind of wish there was some kind of conclusion to that in the outro.

I feel like the lyrics associated with Peter Pan get delivered a little awkwardly. It's like the syllables don't quite fit but they went with those lyrics to fit the theme. The repeat in the bridge is a strange decision.
Ending could've been better, it was a bit abrupt.
Kind of repetitive. Vocals kind of stick out a bit. I don't really like the way the last line of the bridge was delivered.
Lyrics are a little cheesy. Still, there is a story.
I like Adam Levine's vocals in the chorus but he sounds a little rushed by the background. The song is repetitive and the background and lyrics are very basic.

I'm not a fan of this structure rap songs use where they feature an artist to do the repetitive chorus and do all the distinct verses. This is a slightly better example. This one actually follows a consistent theme.
Not a huge fan of the ending. All of the unique verses seem to follow the exact same melody which just feels lazy.

A bit of an odd feeling from how upbeat the background is? Lyrics are more sad and the vocals sound like they're far away, maybe to create a bittersweet feeling? It's on the edge in terms of repetitiveness for me. Distinct verses are good.
Some pretty awkward lyrics such as "I've loved you three summers now" and most of the bridge. I think a few scores could go down here but they're on the edge.

Background feels like the higher voices are a little loud maybe. Very repetitive. The melody frequently ends a phrase sounding unresolved, which isn't always bad but it should probably resolve at some point.
The glaring problem is the 2 minute instrumental break. Long instrumentals aren't always bad, but here it dominates a huge portion of the song and it's at a lower energy level.
Ends abruptly. The song is supposed to be laid back it feels but the vocals still sound kind of lazy. Lyrics are a strange mix of trying to sound genuine while also being very crass.
logs.songName: Magic In The Hamptons (feat. Lil Yachty)

logs.comments: Very repetitive lyrics. The scoop up at the end of "you" and "do" gets a little annoying when it's repeated that many times.

"These are words that go together well" isn't a great line in my opinion. Lyrics get a little repetitive too. Flow score could go down but at least some of the words vary and the outro was pretty nice.
"Giving me a million reasons" just doesn't sound great when repeated I feel, probably because "million" is just an awkward word. Vocals are pretty good on this one though.
Could have benefitted from an outro in my opinion. The song is also just dominated by sections that get repeated.

Some of the lyrics are good but overall there are just a lot of mediocre word choices. "Introvert," "mean," and "crazy bitch" are a few examples. Even the "mmm" instead of an actual word. Some phrases are oddly short.

Lyrics are a bit corny but there are good ones and bad ones. I like the line "I'm only a man with a candle to guide me" and I don't like the line "would you be scared." There aren't any new developments in the song in the second half.
A little repetitive. I'm don't like the lyrics in the chorus that much.
The background vocals by Christina Aguilera in the last chorus help a lot.
logs.songName: Moves Like Jagger - Studio Recording From "The Voice" Performance

logs.comments: I don't really like the pre-chorus, it feels a bit out of place with the rest of the song. I lowered flow a bit because of that combined with the chorus being a bit repetitive.
Melody is a little odd at some points. The introduction is a little awkward too. It ends on another chorus without going anywhere really.

The sad longing vocals don't really fit with some of the incredibly crass lyrics. The pitch correction, especially during the turns, is a bit over the top in my opinion, though I assume it's stylistic.
It's cool how the rap verses kind of set up the chorus with the lines about building up to success.
I absolutely love the transition into the bridge on this song.
I really like the mood the song creates but it is absurdly repetitive.

It sounds like Jay Rock drags a little in his verse. He takes a lot of breaths too. There just isn't a whole lot going on in the background. Rap songs are often like this though, it's just a track put on repeat.

This song does a very good job of capturing an upbeat happy feeling as a part of the Concerto for a Rainy Day. I feel like the chorus and post-chorus feel disjointed and kill the momentum of the song though, probably because the percussion stops.
Maybe gets a little repetitive. I didn't deduct anything.
For its purpose the lyrics were obviously effectively but outside of that context it kind of feels like I'm listening to a scuffle that I have no part in. Background is basic and repetitive.
A lot of "one summer dream" in the lyrics. Vocals in the opener are good but they sound awkward and crude compared to the background for most of the song.

The part of the chorus where there are heavy piano chords sounds a bit disjointed and choppy. Lyrics are a little edgy and "repair" gets repeated. The vocals sound a bit distorted and oscillate unnaturally at a few points.

I'm biased because I like this song. It's weird, unconventional, and just sounds really fun. You could say lyrics like "there is water at the bottom of the ocean" are nonsensical. The story in the lyrics also definitely isn't as happy as the song sounds.

Interesting how the chorus shortens every time. The second chorus is the most confusing, where it goes from "one who understands" to "knows your heart." I kind just don't like how the song has three virtually identical peaks.

Intro is very good. Some lyrics like "golden eagle" and "queen of hearts" feel a bit random because they don't seem to be connected to one theme. The chorus feels a bit out of place. Background, lyrics and cohesion could be scored lower.

The videogame theme was cool, I wish it extended to the later verses. The climax maybe is a bit sudden, I guess that's the idea? He's a good singer but I feel his voice lacks some "purity" as some points. Partially the pitch correction probably.
Lyrics are pretty odd. Background score could arguably be raised, it was a pretty fire guitar solo.
Lyrics are a little odd but the real problem is that there are only two real verses that just get repeated. The delivery is changed and the flow of the song has a clear shape.
Some lyrics are a bit cheesy and some are good. I like the section started with "I should get a cigarette." Lyrics in the bridge are a bit excruciating.

Gun violence is a serious topic but I can't help but find some of the lyrics to be extremely funny. Chorus is a little repetitive, transition out of the instrumental is a bit sudden and the outro doesn't conclude very well.

No clue why this song is called "Princess of China." The flow of the sections is a little odd, especially when it dips to the same "static" noise section from the beginning in the middle of the song. The story in the lyrics just doesn't feel cohesive.
A bit repetitive, there are only two short distinct verses and a very short bridge that don't get repeated. Lyrics feel a bit abstract, like they don't have much further meaning beyond sounding cool.
I don't dislike the rapping but it sounds like rushes a bit at some parts. Chorus repeats a lot. Backing track isn't bad but it's also repetitive as usual.

I feel that the low sections aren't sad enough and the high sections don't sound angry enough to match the story in the lyrics. Lyrics are a little edgy but understandably so given the setting. Sounds like the audio bugs a bit around the 2 minute mark.

Rap verse makes no sense in the context of the song. It talks about how much money he has and how many cars he has but the character in the rest of the song is miserable and doesn't even have enough money for the "payphone."
I like how all the repeated verses have slightly different lyrics. Lyrics are a little cheesy.

Each progressive chorus actually does noticeably peak higher than the last. The added background vocals in the last chorus are actually very nice. I do wish there were more distinct lyrics and verses but generally the lyrics are solid.
Lyrics in the chorus are a little odd but generally they're fine.

I think the choruses get a little louder each time but it's not super obvious. There's a bit of movement in the background too but I still feel it's not quite enough. It's debatable whether or not the flow score should've been lowered.
Pretty repetitive. The line "why you gotta be so rude" also just sounds a bit crude, which I suppose fits the character here, but still just isn't nice to listen to.

That guitar riff goes pretty hard honestly. The beginning is a bit trippy because it kind of baits you into thinking he's going to come in on a different beat than he does. I like the first verse though. The end of the bridge almost sounds like the outro.

I like the lines starting with "a noise in the city" and "down on the corner." It is a little odd how it builds up to the chorus which then is rather low energy. Vocals are a mixed bag. Some lyrics are a little confusing in isolation, mostly in verse 3.

Not a whole lot of meaning in the lyrics and they're pretty repetitive. The song also doesn't really go anywhere, it just ends repeating "meet you all the way." The highlight of the song is mostly just the incredibly instrumental.

Really nice riff. Credit where it's due, the line "there's only one carrot and they all gotta share it" is good. Having "runaway" in the name even though the song says "run away" is interesting. A bit repetitive and it just ends on another chorus.

The rhymes are creative but disjointed. There's a bit of a lisp, not sure if that's specific to this song because of the name. Structure is just one massive run which makes listening to it feels like reading a massive block of unformatted text.
Vocals might have a bit too much energy considering this is about someone dying. Cohesion could arguably be lowered for that.

The lyrics in general are very good, but that one line "Faded like The Beatles on 'Hey Jude'" is disastrous. It doesn't help that the melody is disrupted and paused on that line, which further emphasizes it. I made some pretty harsh deductions for those.
Lyrics are a little basic and cheesy. A few lines sound like they needed a few more syllables, like "for that night" and "needed you most." Instrumental is also pretty basic.
I don't like how it ends by just repeating the chorus more.
Every chorus is virtually identical.
I do like how much "personality" this song has. Parts get added throughout the song which helps the flow. I could see an argument that the cohesion score should be raised.
The audience noises in the background kind of interrupt what feels like a very intimate duet. I think a dedicated outro would've improved this song. In fact, the song generally feels incomplete.
Lyrics are a little basic but I didn't deduct. I deducted from flow because it was a bit repetitive and I didn't like how it just ended on another chorus.

The vocals sound a little garbled in the distinct verses. It's quite repetitive. Not a fan of the Snow White line, it feels petty and the message of that story doesn't seem very similar to the one in this song.
"I want it so fine" is a pretty weird line, and the chorus is just that one line being repeated. The instrumental section is also pretty odd.

The vocals almost have too much detail and are slightly too loud. Not a huge fan of the English lyrics but overall the lyrics are good. Not a big fan of the rap section. I like how the last verse calls back to the first.
logs.songName: Song Request 신청곡 (feat. SUGA of BTS)

logs.comments: I feel like it almost sounds a little too upbeat? I do like the line "would you feel a thing if you saw me right now." I don't like how that version of the chorus gets repeated though, it makes it feel less impactful. The bridge also doesn't quite fit.

I like a lot of parts of this song but I feel that his voice doesn't quite fit. I like pretty much all the lyrics except "I watch the summer stars to lead me home" which feels less related. It could be something personal to him. Each chorus peaks higher.

Not much wrong aside from being a little generic. Definitely a little repetitive. In addition to having three long choruses, each chorus repeats within itself. The delivery of the choruses does change though.

I've heard the criticism that their voice is a bit "whiny" here but I think it fits. The whole song is on the same page about the character being a bit pathetic. I don't hate the flow but there are four repeated choruses.
A huge portion of the song is dominated by choruses but all of the parts transition into each other pretty well so I didn't deduct.

Lyrics are absurdly repetitive. The dance break also doesn't help the flow when listening to the track without the performance. I could be hallucinating but it almost sounds like his first few "I don't know" lines were just slightly flat.
